key_terms: The ordered list of named, typed fields, with nullability and optional metadata, that tells every consumer how to interpret an Arrow table's columns.

A fixed-point type that stores a signed integer coefficient and a declared scale s, so the value is the coefficient divided by 10 to the power s. It represents amounts such as 12.50 exactly, unlike a binary floating-point value.
Precision is the maximum number of decimal digits a decimal type can hold; scale is how many of those digits follow the decimal point.
A field property stating whether a value may be absent. It records that a value can be missing, not why it is missing.
Whether data written with one schema can be read under another without changing its meaning. The chapter rejects an incompatible schema instead of silently coercing values.

worked_examples.title: Sum decimal money without float drift
worked_examples.code:
from decimal import Decimal

import pyarrow as pa
import pyarrow.compute as pc

prices = pa.array([Decimal("12.50"), None, Decimal("7.25")], type=pa.decimal128(9, 2))
print(pc.sum(prices))
print(pc.count(prices), prices.null_count)
print(0.1 + 0.2)
worked_examples.interpretation: The decimal sum prints 19.75 exactly, and the counts show two observed values plus one null, so a mean must divide by two. The float line beside it prints a value just above 0.3, which is the drift a binary float column would carry into a ledger. Check the result type of an aggregate too: a decimal sum can widen precision, and a downstream schema with narrower precision will reject it instead of rounding.

worked_examples.title: Reject a decimal that exceeds declared precision
worked_examples.code:
from decimal import Decimal

import pyarrow as pa

try:
    pa.array([Decimal("123456.789")], type=pa.decimal128(5, 2))
except pa.ArrowInvalid as error:
    print("rejected:", type(error).__name__)
print(pa.array(["001", "1"]).unique().to_pylist())
worked_examples.interpretation: Arrow refuses to store 123456.789 in a decimal with five digits of precision instead of silently truncating it, which is the behavior a contract wants at a boundary. The second line keeps the identifiers 001 and 1 as two distinct strings, a reminder that casting identifiers to integers merges keys that a source system treats as different. Treat a precision error as a schema decision to escalate, not a value to clip.

evidence: Exact real-library outputs checked against small independent records, with explicit rejected inputs.
